about: The English of 1750: every word both apps put on screen, in the manner of Samuel Johnson's Preface to the Dictionary as first printed in 1755. A shadow of copy/en.json, which holds the schema (surface, apps, example); a key missing here falls back to it. Spelling as test/data/en-x-1750.spelling.json; no stage-play archaisms, no capitalised common nouns, and the long s only in app.titlePage. Design: LANGUAGE.md section 6.

readout.sub.coldAssumes.text: about {boil} to boil, as experience has shewn

readout.sub.coldAssumes.more.text: How long, upon the average, water stands on the fire before it boils in earnest, amended by your past timings. Press It boils in earnest to-day, and I shall correct the time while the eggs are cooking.

readout.restored.text: I have taken up this one again after the page was reloaded. The times are true, but I cannot sound the alarm, so watch the clock.

refusal.whiteNeverSets.text: With the heat withdrawn, the water cools before the white is set. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.harderThanPan.text: With the heat withdrawn, this quantity of water ({water}) grows cool before the yolk arrives there. Firmest attainable: {limit}. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.counter.text: An egg left in the open air does not cease to cook because it has ceased to boil. Softest attainable: {limit}. In iced water it might be left softer.

refusal.tap.text: Water from the pump cools the egg too slowly to arrest the yolk. Softest attainable: {limit}. In iced water it might be left a little softer.

refusal.ice.text: Any shorter, and the white is yet raw. Softest attainable for this egg: {limit}.

controls.egg.more.text: A bigger egg takes longer, for the heat has further to go. Eggs differ much; weigh one, therefore, if you can.

controls.measure.legend.text: Or measure it; any one suffices

controls.measure.hint.text: Kitchen scales are the most exact. Wanting them, wrap a slip of paper round the fattest part, and measure the slip.

controls.eggFrom.more.text: Eggs from the fridge give the most certain times, because a fridge is much the same from day to day, and a room is not.

controls.eggFrom.hint.text: I suppose {fridge} for a fridge and {room} for a room. Choose Your own if yours differ.

controls.start.more.text: Boiling water: lower the eggs into water boiling in earnest; they peel more easily. Cold water: the eggs in a cold pan, the fire lit, and press It boils in earnest when the water rolls; the waiting till it boils included, they are done sooner. Sous-vide: I shall tell you how long the eggs require in the water.

controls.afterTheBoil.more.text: Keep it boiling: the water boils in earnest till the eggs come out, and its quantity is of little moment. Fire out, lid on: the eggs once in boiling water, the water finishes them as it cools. This spares fewel; but the quantity of water decides the time, and too little cannot finish the work; measure it therefore.

controls.cooling.more.text: Out of the water, the yolk cooks on for some minutes. Iced water arrests it soonest, and so permits me to offer the softest yolks; the pump is nearly as good. In the open air the egg scarcely cools, and the softest yolks are therefore forbidden.

controls.water.more.text: The quantity of water in the pan, the eggs not reckoned. It signifies chiefly if you put out the fire once it boils, and a little in reckoning how long the water is in boiling.

controls.eggsInPan.more.text: The more cold eggs you put in, the more they cool the water, and the longer they are in cooking. For eggs begun in cold water I have no need of it, for your signal when the water boils already reckons them.

controls.altitude.more.text: The higher you are, the cooler water boils, and the slower eggs cook; upon a mountain, sensibly so.

help.motto.text: Time the egg, and not the minute.

help.how.p1.text: I compute how heat passes into your egg, and how far the yolk and the white are set; and then I choose the time that leaves the yolk as you desired.

help.how.aside.text: I reason by [heat conduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation) through a sphere of the bigness of your egg, and the setting of white and yolk as a dose of heat accumulated over time, by the [Arrhenius equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrhenius_equation). Every constant, with its authority, is in the [README](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#2-the-physical-model).

help.how.p2.text: The time of cooling is to be reckoned as time of cooking, since the egg is yet warm within.

help.how.aside2.text: Still air draws off heat so slowly, that the yolk ends within a fraction of a degree of where it would, had the egg never cooled at all. [README §5](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#5-carryover-the-cooling-step-is-part-of-the-recipe).

help.learn.p1.text: From your answers I learn how you like your yolk, and how your eggs cook; from your signal when the water boils, how long it is in boiling. A single reading of the probe teaches me how fast heat enters your eggs. No question is compulsory.

help.learn.aside.text: I use [sequential Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_filter) to learn your eggs and your taste, with an [ordered probit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordered_probit) for the yolk you had, from rear to hard, and the white about it. I keep a record of every egg; so that when I am improved, I learn again from all of them. [The design](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer/blob/main/INFERENCE.md).

help.reliable.title.text: Of eggs to be relied upon

help.reliable.intro.text: The greatest help is to tell me how each egg came out; after that, all depends upon your manner of cooking.

help.reliable.forYou.text: For the settings as they now stand

help.reliable.every.text: Weigh the egg if you can: one size upon the box comprehends eggs that need very different times. Eggs straight from the fridge are more certain than eggs at the warmth of the room.

help.reliable.hot.text: Of all methods the easiest to perform rightly. Keep the water boiling in earnest the whole time.

help.reliable.cold.text: Press It boils in earnest when the whole surface rolls, not at the first bubbles. By it I correct my time while the eggs are cooking.

help.reliable.heatOff.text: The water does all the cooking; measure it therefore, and be liberal. With too little, the white will never set.

help.reliable.cooling.text: Iced water is the most certain, and the pump nearly as good. Cooling in the open air is but indifferent.

help.odds.p1.text: I cannot promise every egg. Below the figures of the time, I tell you whether this one will probably come out as you desire, and if not, whether too soft or too firm. The bracket below the slider shews the yolks you are likely to have; and the more eggs you tell me of, the narrower it grows.

help.odds.aside.text: Eight eggs in ten will come out within this bracket. I incline to the longer side, since a white left unset is commonly worse than a yolk too firm. The deeper the shading upon the slider, the surer I am of that degree coming out right.

help.unsure.counter.text: The open air. No one appears to have made publick how fast an egg cools in still air, and that is therefore the weakest of my numbers.

help.unsure.heatOff.text: The fire out. I suppose an ordinary pan with its lid on; a heavy pot or a loose lid will alter the time.

help.unsure.white.text: Whites. I cannot distinguish a white that sets late from a cook who calls a tender white unset.

help.unsure.sousVide.text: Sous-vide. Below {floor} the white remains liquid and moves within the shell, which I leave out of my account; there I am not to be trusted. By my reckoning, so cool, the white takes hours, or even days, to set, if it sets at all.

help.sources.intro.text: The chief authorities behind my numbers. The [README](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#10-references) lists them all, with what each has settled.

help.source.williams.text: C. D. H. Williams, “The Science of Boiling an Egg”, University of Exeter (1998). newton.ex.ac.uk/teaching/CDHW/egg (the host is gone; the page is in the Internet Archive)

help.source.buay.text: D. Buay, S. K. Foong, D. Kiang, L. Kuppan and V. H. Liew, “How long does it take to boil an egg? Revisited”, European Journal of Physics 27, 119-131 (2006). doi:10.1088/0143-0807/27/1/013

help.source.abbasnezhad.text: B. Abbasnezhad, N. Hamdami, J.-Y. Monteau and H. Vatankhah, “Numerical modeling of heat transfer and pasteurizing value during thermal processing of intact egg”, Food Science & Nutrition 4, 42-49 (2016). doi:10.1002/fsn3.257

help.source.denys.text: S. Denys, J. G. Pieters and K. Dewettinck, “Computational fluid dynamics analysis of combined conductive and convective heat transfer in model eggs”, Journal of Food Engineering 63, 281-290 (2004). doi:10.1016/j.jfoodeng.2003.06.002

help.source.vega.text: C. Vega and R. Mercadé-Prieto, “Culinary Biophysics: on the Nature of the 6X °C Egg”, Food Biophysics 6, 152-159 (2011). doi:10.1007/s11483-010-9200-1

help.source.weijers.text: M. Weijers, P. A. Barneveld, M. A. Cohen Stuart and R. W. Visschers, “Heat-induced denaturation and aggregation of ovalbumin at neutral pH described by irreversible first-order kinetics”, Protein Science 12, 2693-2703 (2003). doi:10.1110/ps.03242803

help.source.hoyt.text: D. F. Hoyt, “Practical methods of estimating volume and fresh weight of bird eggs”, The Auk 96, 73-77 (1979).

help.source.usda.text: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service, “High Altitude Cooking”.

idle.welcome.text: I begin with the times of an ordinary egg; and as you tell me how each one came out, I fit them to your eggs, and to your taste.

controls.units.more.text: I begin with what is customary where your browser says you are.

controls.thermometer.more.text: When the counting-down of the cooling ends, the middle of the yolk is at its hottest, and I shall ask for one reading. Thrust the point to the very middle, and tell me the highest number you see: anywhere else, or any later, reads lower. That single reading teaches me how fast heat enters your eggs. In the open air nothing is counted down, and I do not ask.

controls.thermometer.ask.text: Ask a reading after every egg

controls.room.more.text: At your pleasure. Hold the probe in the air of your kitchen, and set down what it reads; it signifies most for eggs that have stood in the room, and for eggs cooled in the open air. Leave it empty, and I shall suppose {room}.

outcome.likely.firm.text: Probably as you desire; if not, a little firm.

outcome.likely.soft.text: Probably as you desire; if not, a little soft.

outcome.unsure.text: It may come out too soft or too firm; which, I cannot yet foretell.

outcome.miss.firm.text: It may miss; more likely too firm.

outcome.miss.soft.text: It may miss; more likely too soft.

certainty.time.text: I judge the true time to lie between {low} and {high}.

certainty.help.text: More of my certainty, in the Preface

outcome.whiteRunny.text: The white may yet be unset.

outcome.bracket.text: The bracket below the slider shews where your yolk will probably fall. To be secure against a soft yolk, slide to the right, till the left end of the bracket rests where you would be content; against a firm one, slide to the left, till its right end does.

outcome.why.text: Before your first egg I know neither your taste, nor your eggs, nor your kitchen, and the bracket therefore begins wide. Every egg you tell me of makes it narrower.

outcome.learning.text: To hasten my learning, answer both questions after every egg, and, having begun from cold water, tell me when the water boils in earnest. If you have a probe thermometer, a single reading instructs me most.

advice.toggle.text: How this may be made more certain

advice.fridge.text: Use eggs straight from the fridge: how cold a fridge is I know, but not your room.

advice.weigh.text: Weigh the egg. One size upon the box comprehends eggs that need very different times.

advice.ice.text: Cool the eggs in iced water. In the open air, how much more the yolk will cook is not easily foretold.

advice.moreWater.text: Use more water. With the fire out, more water holds its heat longer, and small differences in its cooling signify less.

learned.literature.text: I have hitherto learned nothing. Tell me how each egg came out, and, having begun from cold water, when the water boils in earnest.

learned.pan.text: {water} of water is about {time} in boiling

learned.forget.more.text: I forget all your measures, and return to the common estimates. A wrong answer or two a few eggs more will wash out; you need this only for some strange mischance.

learned.confirm.message.text: I shall forget all your results, and how long your water was in boiling, and the times return to where they began.

learned.export.none.text: There is nothing yet to copy out.

learning.badge.more.text: You share your results, and so I am yet learning from them. Now and then I move the time some seconds either way, ten at most, to learn what passes just beside the time I would choose. It may leave an egg a little softer or firmer than I would otherwise aim at. Leave off sharing in the settings, and the time stays where I would put it.

share.what.text: I shall send your results, the past too: how every egg was boiled, and how you found it. No name nor place: a cypher drawn at random upon this device stands for you. While this is on, I shall now and then move a time some seconds, to learn the faster.

share.more.text: The results of one kitchen can teach me only of that kitchen; those of many together shew me how eggs, pots, water and cooling truly differ, and the next version of the app begins every one from what they shew. I send the egg’s size, how it was boiled, the heat at which the water boils (which tells roughly how high you dwell), your answers, and what I expected. Moving a time some seconds teaches what the usual times cannot, and keeps within what you would call right. Leave off whenever you please; Expunge the results takes every one from the server.

share.waiting.one: {eggs} more shall go when the server can be reached.
share.waiting.other: {eggs} more shall go when the server can be reached.

share.confirm.message.text: I shall bid the server expunge every result this device has sent, and leave off sharing. What I have learned here remains.

share.deleting.text: Expunging. If the server cannot now be reached, I shall ask again until it answers.

share.deleted.text: Expunged: the server keeps nothing this device sent.

controls.language.more.text: English (1750) is English as Samuel Johnson wrote it. I change to it when you choose Imperial. Should the reader find this stile tiresome, choose English: the modern tongue is restored, and Fahrenheit’s scale kept.

controls.units.period.text: I can likewise write the imperial measures in the English of their day.
